AeglysAIAdaptive Intelligence for Secure & Resilient Distributed Systems

Observe. Assess. Authorize. Respond.

An open-source research initiative exploring explainable, risk-aware and adaptive authorization for secure and resilient cloud-native distributed systems.

Intelligent capabilities can be incorporated into system control loops while remaining bounded by deterministic engineering mechanisms, rather than simply added as an external service.

01 / Research progression

A baseline for every next step.

Three implemented authorization baselines and a completed, experimental offline Model D research implementation.

Explore the models ↗
Model AA

RBAC

Role-based access control establishes the deterministic authorization baseline.

Implemented
Model BB

RBAC + ABAC

Attribute-based conditions extend role-based authorization with request context.

Implemented
Model CC

Contextual Risk

Deterministic contextual risk adds explicit risk rules to role-based authorization.

Implemented
Model DD

Behavioral Adaptive Authorization

The bounded offline research implementation is complete; internal synthetic validation has been performed. Model D remains experimental and non-enforcing.

Research Implementation Complete
A research progression, not a product maturity scale.

Models A–C describe implemented baselines in the separate research repository; this portal does not independently validate their effectiveness. Model D research implementation is complete and non-enforcing (enforcement_authority=NONE), not a production authorization mechanism. Internal synthetic validation does not establish external field effectiveness or commercial readiness. Drift and mock-feedback limitations remain unresolved.

02 / System perspective

Evidence in. Explainable decisions out.

Investigating how identity, context, behavior and system state can inform authorization within explicit policy boundaries.

03 / The central question

What changes when authorization can adapt?

How does explainable, policy-bounded, closed-loop adaptive authorization perform relative to RBAC, ABAC and deterministic risk-aware authorization under behavioral and operational anomalies in cloud-native distributed systems?
